title: Docker builds: layers, identity, and a smaller runtime
outcome: Build a Rails artifact without embedding secrets or relying on mutable tags.
useCase: Rails image delivery and predictable rebuilds.
benefits: Faster repeat builds and clearer runtime boundaries.
drawbacks: Native dependencies, patching, and reproducibility need maintenance.
version: Pinned local examples · version-labelled configuration fragments
cue: Cache stable inputs. Keep secrets out. Let signals reach the app.

trace.title: Build context
trace.detail: A Dockerfile records image construction. Layer caching can speed repeated builds when stable dependency steps occur before frequently changing app files. A .dockerignore keeps unnecessary/private content out of the build context.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Build context → dependency layers → app layer → runtime command → registry digest. Change only a source file and inspect which layers rebuild. Then change a gem lock and predict the invalidation.

During stop, SIGTERM should reach the process so it can stop taking work and finish or abandon it safely within the orchestrator’s grace period.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Deleting a secret in a later layer does not erase it from earlier layers. A mutable base/tag can change rebuild output. A shell that does not exec can interfere with signal forwarding.
